fields.aka: Rāmadāsa, Rāma, Abhirāma Gopāla, Abhirāma Gosvāmī
fields.disappearance: Caitra Kṛṣṇa Saptamī (Abhidhāna: gauṇa Vaiśākha Kṛṣṇa Saptamī, the same day)
fields.notes:
One of the twelve gopālas of Śrī Nityānanda; went with Him to preach in Bengal. Lifted a huge log and held it as a flute (Caitanya-caritāmṛta Ādi 11.16). Married Mālinī Devī by Nityānanda's wish. His obeisances cracked any stone that was not a Deity; seven newborn sons of Nityānanda died from them, Vīrabhadra and Gaṅgā Devī survived. His whip Jaya-maṅgala gave prema (Śrīnivāsa Ācārya). Found the Deity of Gopīnātha at Rāma-kuṇḍa, Khānākula; the Bali Maṭha in Purī is said to be his.

In Kṛṣṇa-līlā: Śrīdāmā (Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā 126); in Rāma-līlā: Bharata (Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇava Abhidhāna). Jagadbandhu Bhadra holds that Rāmadāsa was a form manifested by Abhirāma, not the same person (Abhirāma-līlāmṛta).
Dates/place from B. V. Tīrtha, “Sri Chaitanya: His Associates”, and the Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇava Abhidhāna.

fields.place: Haldā Maheśpur (Jessore, now Bangladesh); some say Bodhkhānā; samādhi in Vṛndāvana
fields.notes:
One of the twelve gopālas; Nityānanda's most intimate servant (Caitanya-caritāmṛta Ādi 11.23). A brahmacārī. In prema he brought a crocodile out of the water and made kadamba flowers bloom on a jambīra tree. His Deity Śrī Kālācāṅd is in Vṛndāvana.

In Kṛṣṇa-līlā: Sudāmā (Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā 127).

Not Sundarānanda Ṭhākura, son and disciple of Gatigovinda and grandson of Śrīnivāsa Ācārya (his own record).
Son and disciple of Gatigovinda, and grandson of Śrīnivāsa Ācārya (Karṇānanda; Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇava Abhidhāna, entry «Sundarānanda» 2). Not the gopāla Sundarānanda Ṭhākura of Nityānanda's branch.

fields.name: Dhanañjaya Paṇḍita
fields.place: Śītala-grāma (Bardhamān), with his samādhi; also Sāṅcaḍā-Pāṅcaḍā and Jalandi; family home Jāḍagrāma (Chittagong), or Siyān-Muluk (Birbhum)
fields.notes:
One of the twelve gopālas of Śrī Nityānanda (Caitanya-caritāmṛta Ādi 11.31; Caitanya-bhāgavata Antya 5.733). Parents: Śrīpati Bandyopādhyāya and Kālindī Devī; or, according to Śrī Gaurāṅga-mādhurī, Ādideva Vācaspati and Dayāmayī Devī. Married Haripriyā, but soon left home; gave all his money to Mahāprabhu and took a begging pot. Younger brother: Sañjaya Paṇḍita of Jalandi (perhaps also his disciple). Cūḍāmaṇi dāsa wrote the Bhuvana-maṅgala from what he heard from him.

In Kṛṣṇa-līlā: Vasudāma (Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā 127).
Dates/place from B. V. Tīrtha, “Sri Chaitanya: His Associates”, and the Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇava Abhidhāna.

fields.name: Gaurīdāsa Paṇḍita
fields.disappearance: Śrāvaṇa Śukla Dvādaśī (the texts: Ekādaśī or Trayodaśī), in Vṛndāvana
fields.place: Ambikā-Kālnā (Bardhamān); earlier Śāligrāma (Nadia); samādhi at Dhīra-samīra, Vṛndāvana
fields.notes:
One of the twelve gopālas of Śrī Nityānanda (Caitanya-caritāmṛta Ādi 11.26-27). Parents: Kaṁsāri Miśra and Kamalā Devī. Brothers: Dāmodara, Jagannātha, Sūryadāsa Sarakhela, Kṛṣṇadāsa (Dīna Kṛṣṇadāsa, the poet) and Nṛsiṁha-Caitanya; uncle of Vasudhā and Jāhnavā Devī. Wife: Vimalā Devī; sons Balarāma and Raghunātha (Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇava Abhidhāna). Mahāprabhu gave him His oar and a Gītā, and stayed with him with Nityānanda as the Deities of Gaura-Nityānanda at Ambikā-Kālnā. His disciple Hṛdaya Caitanya was the guru of Śyāmānanda.

In Kṛṣṇa-līlā: Subala (Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā 128).
Dates/place from B. V. Tīrtha, “Sri Chaitanya: His Associates”, and the Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇava Abhidhāna.

fields.name: Kamalākara Pippalāi
fields.appearance: 1414 Śaka (1492 CE), at Khālijuli near the Sundarbans (family tradition, Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇava Abhidhāna)
fields.disappearance: Caitra Śukla Trayodaśī; 1485 Śaka, at 71 (family tradition); in Vṛndāvana (Vaiṣṇavācāra-darpaṇa)
fields.place: Māheśa (Hooghly), with the Deity of Lord Jagannātha; born at Khālijuli
fields.notes:
One of the twelve gopālas of Śrī Nityānanda (Caitanya-caritāmṛta Ādi 11.24); Nityānanda gave him Saptagrāma (Caitanya-bhāgavata Antya 5.729) or Pāṇihāṭi (Jayānanda). At the Pāṇihāṭi festival (1517) and at Kheturī (1582). Younger brother: Nidhipati. Married late; son Caturbhuja, daughter Rādhārāṇī (married Kāmadeva Paṇḍita of Khaḍadaha) according to his descendants; daughter Vidyunmālā according to the Nityānanda-vaṁśa-vistāra.

In Kṛṣṇa-līlā: Mahābala (Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā 128).

fields.disappearance: Pauṣa Kṛṣṇa Trayodaśī, 1463 Śaka (1541 CE), at the age of 60 (Abhidhāna: Agrahāyaṇa Kṛṣṇa Trayodaśī)
fields.place: Saptagrāma (Hooghly); Uddhāraṇapura near Katwa, with his samādhi
fields.notes:
One of the twelve gopālas of Śrī Nityānanda (Caitanya-caritāmṛta Ādi 11.41). Of a wealthy suvarṇa-vaṇik family; father Śrīkara Datta, mother Bhadrāvatī, son Śrīnivāsa Datta. Dewan of the king of Naihāṭī. Nityānanda stayed with him at Saptagrāma and purified the vaṇik community through him; when Nityānanda could not cook, Uddhāraṇa cooked for Him. He left wealth and family to serve Nityānanda (Abhidhāna; B. V. Tīrtha) — Bhaktivedānta Svāmī says he stayed a householder.

In Kṛṣṇa-līlā: Subāhu (Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā).
Dates/place from B. V. Tīrtha, “Sri Chaitanya: His Associates”, and the Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇava Abhidhāna.
